questions.question: Explain what the ratio 1:50 000 means on a map.
questions.expected_answer: It means that 1 unit of measurement on the map represents 50 000 of the same units on the real ground (e.g., 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm on the ground).

questions.question: Why do we divide by 100 000 when converting our final answer from centimetres to kilometres?
questions.expected_answer: Because there are 100 centimetres in a metre, and 1000 metres in a kilometre. 100 x 1000 = 100 000. So there are 100 000 cm in 1 km.

questions.question: What is the shortcut for finding real distance in kilometres on a 1:50 000 map, and why does it work?
questions.expected_answer: You multiply the map distance in cm by 0,5. It works because 50 000 cm is equal to 0,5 km, meaning every 1 cm on the map is exactly half a kilometre in reality.
